annotations.text:
SENSEE-I student flow, left to right.

shadcn token values: #09090b foreground, #71717a muted, #e4e4e7 border, #f4f4f5 muted surface. 8px cards, 6px controls, 36px buttons. Geist.

Static mockups: each screen is one representative moment.

Mid-session: State passed, Elaborate on attempt 2 of 3.

Step position is the four ticks in the header. Attempts are the three dots on the step divider. Criteria are named inside the message rather than in a separate row.

Shipped. The reading is a rendered PDF page.

Table 3.1 survives the format, which is the point: the student can cite a figure the extracted text would have flattened. The extracted text is still what the agents grade against.

Same content, two containers.

3 is a full page, 3b is a dialog over the reading list.

Both carry the Scenario chip: never attempted, completed, all failed, mixed.

Between choosing a reading and the session starting.

The student reads first and says so explicitly; there is no automatic advance. The button is never disabled, because scrolling is not reading and a gate would prove nothing.

No session exists yet. It is created when this button is pressed.

A was chosen. The tutor stops naming the criteria in its sentence as of prompt v2, and the interface labels them instead.

C and D are kept because they are the cheap options: they need nothing from the backend, since the tutor already says the names out loud.

Instructor flow. Classes are a name and a section, shown to students as one label.

Removing a student or deleting a class takes access away, not data: the sessions stay for the study.
